Package com.stzteam.features.robotlocalization.vio.sim

Class QuestOriginFrame

java.lang.Object
com.stzteam.features.robotlocalization.vio.sim.QuestOriginFrame
public class QuestOriginFrame extends Object
The headset's origin frame, and what happens to it when a POSE_RESET arrives.

This is the point of this feature that is easy to get wrong, the equivalent of the sign of tx in the simulated Limelight. It lives in its own class, with pure tests, for that reason.

The misunderstanding it prevents

A Quest does not publish the robot's field pose. It publishes the headset's pose in an arbitrary origin of its own, the place where it was when the app started. Making that origin coincide with the field origin is something the robot code has to cause, by calling setPose(). If the simulation published the field pose directly, it would be hiding exactly the step most teams skip.

The arithmetic

If the Quest's origin is at field pose O and the headset is physically at H, what gets published is H seen from O: 
published = H.relativeTo(O)
A POSE_RESET to T asks that, without moving the headset, what is published becomes T. Solving the equation above for O: 
O = H ∘ T⁻¹

  • Method Details

    • randomized

      public static QuestOriginFrame randomized(double translationMeters, double rotationDegrees, Random random)
      Creates a frame with a randomly displaced origin, to force the robot code to do its seeding properly. With the origin at identity, a team that never calls setPose() sees correct field poses by accident and the bug does not show up until competition.
      Parameters:
      translationMeters - maximum displacement in metres.
      rotationDegrees - maximum yaw deviation in degrees.
      random - the randomness source, so the test stays reproducible.
      Returns:
      a frame with an arbitrary origin.

    • reset

      public void reset(edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Pose3d headsetFieldPose, edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Pose3d targetPose)
      Re-anchors the origin so a headset physically at headsetFieldPose starts reporting targetPose. This is what a real POSE_RESET does.
      Parameters:
      headsetFieldPose - the headset's real field pose.
      targetPose - the pose the robot code wants the Quest to report.
